title: Greek Mint and Oregano Meatballs with Tzatziki
changes_from_base: Beef and lamb mixture flavoured with fresh mint, dried oregano, cumin and lemon zest, bound with water-soaked bread; shaped slightly flattened and shallow-fried in olive oil, served with tzatziki and lemon instead of simmering in tomato sauce; no parmesan.
summary: This follows the same method as our classic meatballs, but a beef and lamb mixture is flavoured with mint, oregano, cumin and lemon zest, shaped slightly flattened, shallow-fried in olive oil, and served with tzatziki and lemon instead of simmered in tomato sauce.

ingredients.item: day-old white bread, crusts removed, torn small
small onion, coarsely grated, juice squeezed out
fine sea salt or table salt
small cucumber (about 150 g), coarsely grated and squeezed dry
fine sea salt or table salt
lemon, cut into wedges, to serve

steps.title: Make the tzatziki
steps.text: Squeeze the grated cucumber hard in a clean tea towel to remove as much water as possible, which keeps the finished sauce thick rather than watery. Stir it through the yoghurt with the garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, dill and the tzatziki salt, then chill until needed.

steps.title: Mix the meatballs
steps.text: Soak the torn bread in the water for 2 minutes and mash to a paste. Add both minces, the squeezed grated onion, egg, mint, parsley, oregano, cumin, garlic, lemon zest, and the meatball salt and pepper, then knead with your hand for 1-2 minutes until well combined and tacky. Rest the mixture in the fridge for 15 minutes so the bread hydrates fully and the herbs have time to flavour the meat.

steps.title: Shape the meatballs
steps.text: With wet hands, roll the mixture into 16-18 balls of about 50g each, then flatten slightly to around 4cm across. A flatter shape cooks through evenly in a frying pan, without needing a long, slow simmer to reach the centre.

steps.title: Fry and serve
steps.text: Heat the olive oil in the large frying pan over medium heat and fry the meatballs in two batches for 10-12 minutes, turning every 2-3 minutes, until deep brown on all sides and a probe thermometer in the centre reads 71°C. Drain briefly on paper, then serve hot or warm with the tzatziki and lemon wedges.

tips: Squeeze the onion and cucumber properly dry — skipping this step is the most common reason these meatballs or the tzatziki end up watery.
Flattening the meatballs slightly before frying helps them cook through to 71°C without the outside overbrowning.
Turn the meatballs regularly rather than leaving them on one side, so all the surfaces pick up colour evenly.
Let the mixture rest in the fridge for the full 15 minutes; it firms up enough to shape cleanly and holds together better in the pan.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Keeps in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 3 days; store the tzatziki separately and use within 2 days. The meatballs freeze well for up to 2 months, but the tzatziki does not. Reheat the meatballs gently in a covered pan or the oven until piping hot throughout (74°C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
